note: Adapted from Desneux's 1905 original description (in English, with the Latin name), original name Termes (Eutermes) gracilirostris n. sp., including the soldier and worker; the original uses an asterisk '*' as the decimal point (e.g. 3*5 mm), transcribed here as 3.5 mm. Type locality Friedrich-Wilhelmshafen, New Guinea.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head ochre, pale yellowish brown, about 1.5 mm long and less than 0.9 mm wide, rounded posteriorly and narrowing anteriorly, nasus long and slender, in the same plane as the front of the head; pronotum far narrower than the head, saddle-shaped, the anterior part short and high with an almost entire margin; abdomen elongate-oval, tergites pale ochre, without styli. Similar in colour and size to the Australian T. magnus, but the latter has 14-segmented and much longer antennae with segment 4 about equal to segment 3, and a much broader wing in the alate.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldier (nasute): body length to the tip of the nasus 3—3.5 mm. Head ochre, pale yellowish brown, about 1.5 mm long and less than 0.9 mm wide, rounded posteriorly, narrowing anteriorly, nasus long and slender, in the same plane as the front of the head. Antennae 12-segmented, segment 3 slightly longer than or about equal to segment 2 but more slender; segment 4 about equal to segment 3 but wider; individuals with 13 segments also occur, segment 3 about equal to segment 2 but longer than segment 4, segment 4 short and more or less circular. Pronotum far narrower than the head, saddle-shaped, the anterior part short and high, the margin almost entire. Abdomen elongate-oval, tergites pale ochre. No styli.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Worker: body length 3.5—4 mm. Head pale ochre-white, rounded. Antennae short, 14-segmented, segment 2 longer than segment 3, segment 3 short; some appear 13-segmented, with segment 3 divided into two small rings that are not completely separated. Clypeus hardly projecting. First mandibular tooth not larger than the following teeth. Pronotum saddle-shaped, narrower than the head. Abdomen greyish from the intestinal contents.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Locality: Friedrich-Wilhelmshafen, New Guinea, collected in the 1st month (January) of 1901. The original places the species in Haviland's regulus group.
